items.title: Benny Waters interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: they did just like Ella Fitzgerald did with Chick Webb, you know, lifted them right on up higher and higher, you know?

ctx.x: Yeah. Ninety years, wow. Have you have occasion during your many years of experience, to work with either Count Basie or Joe Williams?

No I haven’t. No I haven’t. I wish I did. But I tell you I did work with a band that, well I may be saying something that people will agree, you know, but I had a pleasure working with Jimmie Lunceford and I thought it was a greater band than Count Basie. Not musically. Not musically. Exclusive musically. But for all around entertaining and music combined, I think it was a better band than Count Basie. So I had the pleasure of working with Jimmie a couple of years, I mean Jimmie Lunceford see. And I worked with…
Oh that’s marvelous. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee mentions Chick Webb only in the context of another musician (Joe Steele) who played with him. The interviewee does not claim to have met, worked with, or known Chick Webb personally.

ctx.x: Joe Steele, by the way, is the same Joe Steele who later played with Chick Webb -

That's the one, that worked with Chick Webb, see, exactly. And he - some people say he played too much piano, you know, some people said. But that's from his knowledge up there in the school where he studied. And used to arrange, and they said the same thing about his arrangements, said 'Too crowded', you know, the arranging. If you have a tendency to make a lot of notes when you play, you're taught, the arranger - you do the same thing. See, that's the difference between, the same point - this is like Sy Oliver…
You met Johnny Hodges in Boston.
